name: Cogent Communications, Inc.

profile.reading: This is a Cogent Communications data center in Phoenix, Arizona, part of Cogent Communications Holdings network, though no source checked this session disclosed a specific street address, power capacity, or square footage for this particular Phoenix building, an honest gap this registry records rather than estimates. Cogent Communications was founded in 1999 by David Schaeffer, who remains chief executive, launching at the height of the dot-com era with backing from angel investors including members of Keiretsu Forum, and is headquartered in Washington, D.C. Within its first three years the company pursued an aggressive acquisition strategy, reportedly acquiring 13 failing telecommunications carriers and purchasing about 14 billion dollars in capital assets, including roughly 4 billion dollars in property, plant, and equipment, for a combined 60 million dollars between 2001 and 2004, including the major United States assets of PSINet and the LambdaNet operations in France and Spain. Cogent operates a large scale internet backbone network carrying more than 100 terabits per second of traffic under its own Autonomous System Number 174, reported about 1,947 employees and 940.9 million dollars in revenue as of 2023, and offers colocation services within data centers as part of its broader network and hosting business, of which this Phoenix facility is one location.

reading: Cogent Communications Holdings is a publicly traded multinational internet service provider and Tier 1 network operator, listed on NASDAQ under ticker CCOI and filing with the SEC under CIK 0001158324. Cogent's core business is IP transit and network connectivity delivered over its own fiber backbone, and its Phoenix, Arizona facility functions as a network point of presence and small colocation data center supporting that network business, with third-party directories placing its capacity at roughly 12 megawatts. Unlike the wholesale and hyperscale developers elsewhere in this registry, Cogent's data center facilities exist primarily to support its own network operations and to offer colocation to customers who want to connect directly to Cogent's IP transit service, rather than functioning as a standalone real estate leasing business. As a publicly traded, SEC-reporting company, Cogent's overall corporate financials are well documented, though facility-specific capacity figures for individual sites like Phoenix are drawn from third-party data center directories rather than Cogent's own public disclosures, which focus on network and financial metrics rather than site-level specifications.
